title: NAEP, The Nation's Report Card (NAEP Data Service)
agency: National Center for Education Statistics (U.S. Department of Education), for the National Assessment Governing Board
questions: percent of 8th graders proficient in math
achievement gap by race or school lunch eligibility
how a state compares with the national average
NAEP results for a large city district

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (each returns JSON; save it under the name shown) and upload the files. Without the links: the NAEP Data Explorer (https://www.nationsreportcard.gov/ndecore/landing) builds the same tables (choose subject, grade, jurisdictions, variables, statistics; Download > Excel); upload the export and say which table it is. The report cards at https://www.nationsreportcard.gov/ give the headline numbers with significance marks.

cache.why: Small queries; results change only when a new assessment is released (about every two years), but data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: NAEP results are published by NCES, a U.S. government agency; its materials are in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105) unless marked otherwise, and NCES asks that the source be cited.

citation: U.S. Department of Education, Institute of Education Sciences, National Center for Education Statistics, National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP), {dataset}, NAEP Data Service (nationsreportcard.gov), retrieved {retrieved_long}.

audit_hooks.why: NAEP scores are sample estimates with standard errors; a report must say whether differences are statistically significant (NAEP's own tests), not compare point estimates.

clarify: Which subject, grade(s) and year(s)? Default: reading and mathematics, grades 4 and 8, the latest year and 2019 (pre-pandemic).
Average scale score or achievement level (percent at or above Proficient)? They can move differently; default: report both.
Public schools only (NP, the comparison base for states) or all schools (NT)? Default NP when states are involved.
